jurisdiction.venue: Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin), Bonn & Munich

headline: Germany’s Watchdog Finds ‘Serious and Recurring’ Money-Laundering Lapses at State Street’s Munich Bank—and Orders a Remediation Plan
deck: BaFin cited State Street Bank International GmbH for six categories of Money Laundering Act and Banking Act violations, from transaction monitoring to outsourcing controls, without announcing a monetary fine.

score_provenance.rationale: BaFin cited State Street Bank International GmbH for numerous serious and recurring GwG and KWG anti-money laundering violations while imposing €0 in monetary fines, requiring no admission, and charging zero individuals.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: BaFin ordered State Street Bank International GmbH in Munich to submit a remediation plan and progress reports over serious, recurring AML violations across six compliance pillars, with €0 fine announced and zero executives sanctioned.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Repeatedly failing mandatory health and safety inspections across six kitchen stations at a neighborhood diner
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Immediate municipal fines and temporary permit suspension pending re-inspection

sources.title: State Street Bank International GmbH: BaFin orders comprehensive remediation of shortcomings

interactive_art_spec.caption: Headquarters of Germany’s Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) in Bonn. On Nov. 20, the regulator ordered Munich-based State Street Bank International GmbH to submit a remediation plan for recurring anti-money laundering deficiencies.
